design.error_kernel: symmetric categorical full-support iid error conditional on ecological world, field and global assay-quality world
design.pairwise_risk_metric: equal-prior binary pairwise Bayes error upper bound <= BC/2
design.assay_fields: frozen Phase-VII canonical ecological assay fields for each fiber

main_findings: Full-support stochastic assay error preserves overlap between same-quality target-discordant hypotheses at every finite repeat depth, so exact support-based robust separation occurred in 0/67 fibers.
Independent repetition nevertheless reduced the worst target-discordant pair Bhattacharyya error upper bound below 0.05 in every frozen fiber by n<=30.

The required repeat burden was target-structured: climate required 8 repeats in every fiber, biotic stress required 27 in every fiber, and barrier restoration required 11 repeats in one fiber and 27 in five.
Quality calibration did not reduce the minimum repeat depth in any fiber and produced zero strict total synthetic action-cost savings.

H4 was refuted because the limiting pair at the threshold was always a same-quality pair, specifically within-quality ecological target ambiguity rather than uncertainty over which quality world applied.

Phase VII and Phase VIII therefore expose different observational failure modes: fixed systematic miscoding can make explicit calibration structurally necessary, whereas iid full-support random error can be reduced probabilistically by replication while never restoring exact finite-world robustness.
claim_boundary: The 0.7/0.9 quality worlds and symmetric categorical kernels are synthetic fixtures, not calibrated assay models.
BC/2 is a pairwise upper bound under equal priors, not an exact multiclass decision error or posterior probability.
Finite-repeat exact robustness and probabilistic low-risk distinguishability are different inferential claims and must not be conflated.
Synthetic action counts are not monetary, temporal, logistical or ethical field costs.
Quality calibration is idealized and its lack of benefit here follows the frozen worst-pair criterion; it is not a general claim that assay calibration is useless.
The result does not alter Phase-I through Phase-VII or any frozen EOG-WF/BAM manuscript.
